old_caption: The video presents a single, static shot of a collection of colorful gemstones arranged on a white, reflective surface. The gems, including blue, pink, and red varieties, are cut into different shapes, and their facets catch the light, creating reflections and highlights on the surface below. The background is bright and out of focus, ensuring the focus remains on the gemstones. The overall effect is one of polished color and light, emphasizing the beauty of these precious stones.
original_wisa_caption: The video showcases a series of close-up shots featuring a collection of colorful gemstones, primarily diamonds, arranged on a reflective surface. The gems are displayed in various colors, including blue, pink, and red, each cut into a round brilliant cut, which enhances their sparkle and brilliance. The camera pans around the gems, capturing their facets and the way light interacts with them, creating a mesmerizing display of reflections and highlights. The background is softly blurred, ensuring the focus remains on the gemstones. As the camera moves, it occasionally zooms in to highlight specific details of the gemstones, such as their clarity and the precision of their cuts. The overall effect is one of elegance and luxury, emphasizing the beauty and value of these precious stones.
caption: The video showcases a close-up 3D render of faceted gemstones set against a bright, near-white background. A deep-blue faceted stone, a colorless diamond, and a round pink-red gem form the sharp central cluster, while larger blurred gems frame them. As the viewpoint drifts, the blue stone's apparent tilt changes, making its crown look more upright and its facet pattern shift. The pink gem also changes angle slightly, moving a little away from the white stone while retaining its round silhouette. Star-shaped glints flicker across the stones, appearing more often on the pink gem early and on the blue gem later. The background shapes slide past the cluster, with the red mass at lower left growing and shifting outward while the cluster shifts orientation in view.

This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
